newsitem.title: USA: Russia's Dubinin sees 20-24 pct 1996 inflation.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Dubinin sees 20-24 pct 1996 inflation.

text.p: Russia's central bank chairman Sergei Dubinin said he expects a general Russian inflation rate of about 20 to 24 percent in 1996.

Speaking to an investor conference here, Dubinin also said that the official forecasts of the government and the central bank put inflation near 10 percent in 1997, with an economic growth rate of about 2.0 percent.
"We can predict with very good certainty that (the) general inflation rate for this year will be about 20 to 24 percent," Dubinin said.
Dubinin noted that current Russian inflation compares favorably with that of 1995, which exceeded 130 percent, and to the early 1990s hyperinflation rates near 2,000 percent annually.
While acknowledging that 1997 economic growth will be modest at best, the central bank chairman hailed the arrival of a "new stage" in Russia's economic development.
He added that this new economic stage will bring new opportunities for corporations and foreign investors.
Dubinin said he expects exports and manufacturing to lead the way toward positive economic growth next year.
"We have a stable situation in our main export sectors, but nowadays we can (also) predict some substantial growth in the manufacturing sectors."
He also noted the service sector will continue to augment growth in 1997, citing telecommunications specifically.
Responding to a question from the audience, Dubinin called for tax reform and increased enforcement on tax collection.
"We need simplification of the (tax) rules to be more logical and, in some ways, we need a new approach of a very strong political will for the tax collection."
